links.title: Ushiro-kesa-gatame on the IJF technique reference

alt.en: Illustrated sequence of Ushiro-kesa-gatame, the reverse scarf hold.

image.source: Compiled club reference document supplied by the project owner; original source not recorded

about.en: The scarf hold facing the other way: tori sits at uke's right shoulder facing their feet, uke's arm trapped, weight through the chest. A natural landing after some turnovers and armlock entries.

en: Face their feet, hip tight against their shoulder
Trap their right arm under your right armpit
Legs wide and braced; ride their bridge with your hips
Your partner lies on their back; sit beside their right shoulder facing towards their feet, your right hip against their shoulder.
Trap their right arm under your right armpit and pin it against your side, gripping cloth at their sleeve or shoulder.
Lay your left forearm across their body or grip their belt, and lower your chest onto their chest from this reversed angle.
Spread your legs wide along the mat, one forward and one back, soles ready to post.
Hold with heaviness through the chest; when they bridge towards you, sink your hip, and when they turn away, follow around with your legs.

receiving.en: The weight arrives facing the wrong way: their hip is at your shoulder and their legs are up past your head, which makes the usual bridge-and-turn feel unfamiliar. Work your trapped arm and turn towards the gap under their chest; keep your breathing low, and tap clearly if you are held and need to stop.

viNotes.en: The reversed angle is disorienting without sight, so use a landmark: their shoulder against your hip with their arm trapped under your armpit means you are facing their feet. Read a bridge through your hip and a turn through your chest, and answer both with your legs. The weight stays down while you travel around them.

cue.en: The scarf hold facing the other way: the attacker sits at the opponent's shoulder facing their feet, the arm trapped.
